To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found three different lattice operators which measure the intrinsic width of chromoelectric flux tubes and that these operators consistently give the same result for pure SU(2) gauge theory and the Ising model in 2+1 dimensions.

the width of the chromo-electric flux tube in pure SU(2) LGT in (2+ 1) dimensions diverges at the deconfining phase transition and that the intrinsic width can be measured by the three different lattice operators proposed in this work.

we have proposed three lattice operators to measure, in finite temperature LGT, the width ξI of a chromoelectric flux-tube and that we have found the same result, using all three lattice operators, for SU(2)- and Ising-GTs in the vicinity of their deconfinement transitions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the chromoelectrical flux tube in the deconfined phase of pure SU(2) gauge theories in 3d.
the study of the intrinsic width ξ of the chromoelectromagnetic flux tube in pure gauge theories at finite temperature.
the study of the chromoelec- tric flux tube at finite temperature in the deconfined phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chromoelectric field is not confined within a finite tube of thickness ξI, and therefore the string tension is not a physical observable.
the flux tubes in finite temperature LGT are very narrow, with widths that vanish as the decon-finement transition is approached, but that their intrinsic widths are not zero.
the intrinsic width ξ I of the chromoelectromagnetic flux tube diverges at the deconfining phase transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intrinsic width diverges as $ {1/\sqrt {\sigma (T)}} $.
, for the first time, we have measured the intrinsic width of a chromoelectric flux-tube in a finite temperature lattice gauge theory.
, in the deconfined phase of the LGT, the flux tube is a thin string with an intrinsic width which diverges as $ T\to {T_c} $.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intrinsic width can be calculated on a lattice using a simple operator, which can be used as an observable to characterize the flux tube in the deconfined phase.

the intrinsic width is an observable that can be measured in LGTs, and that its behavior near the deconfining transition is consistent with the picture that the deconfinment transition can be understood in terms of an infinite string tension.
we have developed an efficient way to measure ξI on the lattice.
